title: Deployment scouting journal and cadence matrix — July 2026 (WIP)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a compact field-journal for the upcoming midweek rollout. Primary goal: capture short-form observations from small-batch canaries, decide cadence adjustments, and produce an annotated hourly handoff for on-call stewards. Treat as working notes; will be distilled into the formal release notes and ops brief after signoff.

High-level plan (three lanes):
- Scout lane (0–2% traffic): smoke + basic telemetry, live for 30m blocks, quick rollback on signal.
- Expand lane (2–20%): enable KV caching, watch latency p95 and error-rate drift. 90m blocks.
- Ramp lane (20–100%): full rollout with throttles and regional pinning. Continuous watch.

Cadence matrix (recommended starting template):
- T0: deploy canary to subset cluster (tag: canary-scoped). Wait 5m for pod stabilization. Run smoke tests.
- T5m: rudimentary traffic soak (10rps), validate 200/latency < 400ms.
- T30m: telemetry snapshot (p50/p95/p999), KV hit ratio, OOM/CPU spikes. If any of the fail conditions tripped -> rollback.
- Expand windows: 90m soak per percent milestone (2, 5, 10, 20). Operator decision points at each milestone.

Signal thresholds (hard stop triggers):
- 5xx rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m
- p95 latency increases > 2x baseline for 10m
- error pattern change (new error class) observed in >3% of traces
- memory growth trend that is monotonic over 3 collection cycles

Soft signals (require human review):
- p50 drift > 20% but p95 stable
- token generation cost spike without QoR regressions
- slightly elevated tail latencies localized to one AZ

Operator checklist (scouting shift, terse):
- Confirm canary image tag + checksum in release ticket
- Validate health checks and readiness probes (curl /health)
- Run smoke script: smoke-basic.sh (list of endpoints included)
- Collect baseline snapshot: telemetry-query baseline-7d
- Start canary, mark in PagerDuty channel with timestamp
- At 10m: post datapoint summary (p50/p95/errors/KV-hit) in #deploy-watches
- At decision point: annotate decision and reason in release ticket; if rolling back, include snapshot id and pod logs link

Rollback quick recipe:
- Step 0: Pause traffic shifts, mark rollback in comms
- Step 1: Scale down new replica set to 0, scale previous RS to desired count
- Step 2: Verify /health on previous pods, confirm traffic back to baseline
- Step 3: Capture forensic artifacts: pod logs (last 2m), tracing spans (sample ids), heap profiles if applicable
- Step 4: Open an incident stub and notify CS if customer-facing impact noted

Telemetry snippets to run (examples we use during scouting):
- latency-agg: SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 50,95,999) FROM requests WHERE cluster = 'canary' SINCE 30m
- error-signal: count(error_type) GROUP BY error_type WHERE code >= 500 SINCE 15m
- kv-health: avg(kv_hits / kv_lookups) WHERE model = 'mix-v2' SINCE 60m

Communication templates (short):
- Canary start: "Canary started: image redwood/api@sha2345 — 0.5% traffic to cluster eu-west-1. Watchlist open in #deploy-watches. Lina on steward for first 90m."
- Expand note: "Expanding to 5% after 90m soak — p95=210ms, 5xx=0.08%. Proceeding per cadence matrix. Omar to lead next window."
- Rollback notice: "Rolling back canary image redwood/api@sha2345 due to sustained 5xx spike. Reverted to redwood/api@sha2339. Forensics: link->logs. SEV ticket opened: JIRA-RELEASE-821."

Open questions / unknowns to resolve before final run:
- Should we enable prefix-KV caching at the scout lane or only at expand? Tradeoff: caching reduces tokens but hides regressions tied to generation.
- Are our tracing sampling rates sufficient for quick triage (current: 10%)? Consider bump to 25% during ramp windows.
- Can we add a short-lived synthetic load that mimics long-sequence sessions (200 tokens) during expand lane? Need infra approval.

Post-run distillation notes (what to capture into final release notes):
- Exact image tag + commit + infra diff summary
- Canary timeline with annotated decision reasons and timestamps
- Any QoR (quality) regressions and evaluation prompt set used
- Cost-impact note if batching or quantization changed

Attachment/appendix pointers (operational snippets):
- smoke-basic.sh (endpoint list) — check in infra repo PR 452
- telemetry queries — paste into runbook query set CONFLUENCE-ENG-1423

Notes to self (Lina):
- Keep this doc minimal and timestamp entries when making decisions. Use 'decision:' prefix.
- After this run, create a compact 1-pager for CS summarizing customer-impact risk assessment.

Recent field observations (from dry-run on 2026-06-28):
- Minor p95 blip localized to a single AZ after warmup; resolved after pod rotation.
- KV hit ratios improved when we warmed cache with synthetic prefixes — consider warming step in scout lane.

Next steps and owners:
- Priya: confirm tracing sampling change + cost estimate (due 2026-07-09)
- Omar: coordinate infra approval for synthetic long-session load (due 2026-07-10)
- Lina: consolidate run notes and produce final release brief (due 24h after rollout)

-- end of journal entry --
